Tonic and polar covalent compounds are most likely to be soluble in water. Because water is polar, the partial charges in water molecules are able to interact with the charges, either ionic or dipole-induced, in other substances. Ions must be present in an aqueous solution for it to conduct an electric current. Ions come from ionic compounds or from other electrolytes such as acids and bases.

If NO and Br, are placed in a container, molecules of NO and molecules of Br, will react to form NOBr. Some of the NOBr molecules will decompose and the resulting NO and Br, molecules will recombine with different NO and Br, molecules. In this sense, the reaction is dynamic because the original NO and Br, pairings do not remain permanently attached to each other. Eventually, the rate of the forward reaction (combination of NO and Br») will equal the rate of the reverse reaction (decomposition of NOBr) at which point the reaction is said to have reached equilibrium. If you could take “snapshot” pictures of the molecules at equilibrium, you would see a constant number of reactant (NO, Br) and product molecules (NOBr), but the pairings would not stay the same. 4.106 a) Fe(s) + 2 H'(aq) > Fe?"(aq) + Hx(g) ON: 0 +1 +2 0 -3 2+ 232+: b) Fe®* ions = (737 g Sauce) 49 mg Fe |; 10~g }{ 1 mol Fe }{ 1 mol Fe 6.022 x 10™ Fe~“ions 125 g Sauce }\ 1 mg }\ 55.85 g Fe }\_ 1 mol Fe 1 mol Fe?* = 3.11509 x 107! = 3.1 x 10”!
